A 36-year-old man with HIV and recently diagnosed Burkitt lymphoma presents with concerning
symptoms two days after receiving chemotherapy. His symptoms include nausea, vomiting, abdominal
distension, oliguria, hematuria, and lethargy. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 100.1°F,
pulse of 118/min, blood pressure of 144/77 mm Hg, and respiratory rate of 25/min. Notable findings
include jugular venous distension, bibasilar crepitations, bilateral ankle edema, abdominal distension,
and bilateral flank tenderness. Laboratory results show: Na: 141 mmol/L K: 6.5 mmol/L HCO3: 20
mmol/L BUN: 38 mg/dL Cr: 2.1 mg/dL Ca: 7.5 mg/dL Mg: 1.2 mg/dL Phos: 7.6 mg/dL Uric acid: 14.0
mg/dL Which preventive treatment could have reduced the likelihood of developing his current
condition? Answer Choices: (A) Prophylactic calcium gluconate (B) Pre-treatment with sodium
bicarbonate (C) Pretreatment with IV rasburicase (D) Pretreatment with IV calcium gluconate (E)
Pretreatment with a thiazide diuretic (F) Prophylactic plasmapheresis (G) Pre-treatment with
acetazolamide (H) Prophylactic hemodialysis (I) Pre-hydration with alkaline fluids (J) Administration of
kayexalate
 A. Pretreatment with a thiazide diuretic
B. Prophylactic plasmapheresis
C. Pretreatment with IV calcium gluconate
D. Pretreatment with IV rasburicase
E. Pre-hydration with alkaline fluids
F. Prophylactic hemodialysis
G. Administration of kayexalate
H. Prophylactic calcium gluconate
I. Pre-treatment with sodium bicarbonate
J. Pre-treatment with acetazolamide
